rows.why: Item 12 asks how step keywords and step text are handled. The scenario wants the keyword kept as written and the text taken after the keyword and one space. The call kept And, But and * as written. For 'Given   spaced text' it returned '  spaced text', so only the one space after the keyword was dropped and the extra leading spaces stayed. That matches, even though the sentence says 'Trims step text'.

Item 2 asks whether text that isn't a step, under a Feature, Background or Scenario header, counts as description. S2 allows description only between 'Feature:' and the first Background, Scenario or tag line. Text under a Scenario is therefore not description. The implementation skips it anyway: 'more desc' under Scenario: S was ignored and the error only came at line 6, not line 4.

Item 4 asks how Background steps are returned. They come back in a separate feature.background array and are not copied into the scenarios. The call shows background [Given b] while scenario S holds only its own step, which is what S3 expects.

Item 7 asks how tables and doc strings are parsed. The call gives the doc string with the opening quotes' indent removed ('  indented', 'x'), table cells trimmed, and both attached to the step before them. That matches S4.

S5 covers several errors. Item 9 is the closest match because its question is about which line the error is reported at, and S5 is about error lines. An unclosed doc string should fail at the line that opened it. The call threw a ParseError at line 4, the opening quotes, with '(line 4)' in the message.
No item asks whether a feature with no scenarios is valid. Item 1 is about a file with no Feature: line, and item 4 is about an empty Background block, so neither covers this.
